source.title: The Pitfalls of Memorization: When Memorization Hurts Generalization
source.authors: Reza Bayat; Mohammad Pezeshki; Elvis Dohmatob; D. Lopez-Paz; Pascal Vincent

record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own results on memorization and generalization, and argues that memorization can be benign, harmful, or catastrophic depending on the data and learning dynamics. It does not test the claim versions about random labels, unstructured inputs, or the specified label-noise sweep.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Zhang et al. (2021) for fitting completely random labels; that cited result is not this study's result. Table 1 compares subpopulation-shift methods and does not test the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study's own results concern memorization of correctly labeled minority examples under spurious correlations, Waterbirds self-influence, and additive-noise regression. None measures a listed version in the specified kind of system. Completely random-label fitting is cited from Zhang et al.; the paper does not provide its own test of it. These related results do not justify T5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors argue that spurious correlations combined with memorization can drive training loss to zero before robust patterns are learned. They propose MAT to improve generalization under subpopulation shifts and distinguish benign, harmful, and catastrophic consequences of memorization.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies memorization in synthetic spurious-correlation and regression setups, and measures self-influence on Waterbirds; it does not reproduce the original random-label experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome varies with the presence and level of example-specific features; in the regression setup, σϵ = 10−4, 10−3, and 0.0 yield different memorization and generalization behavior.

fits_no_version.finding: ERM learns spurious features first and can then memorize correctly labeled minority examples using example-specific dimensions, preventing core-feature learning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Example-specific features can enable minority-example memorization that obstructs robust learning under spurious correlations.

fits_no_version.finding: With fixed additive target noise, different levels of example-specific input features produce benign fitting, incomplete signal recovery, or catastrophic overfitting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The generalization consequences of interpolation depend on the available features and learning dynamics.

fits_no_version.finding: Waterbirds minority examples have higher estimated self-influence under ERM; MAT reduces and equalizes these scores.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Estimated example dependence varies across subpopulations and training methods under subpopulation shift.

fits_no_version.finding: With two spurious features, ERM gives chance performance on minority test samples, while MAT nearly perfectly classifies all groups.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Memorization-aware training can improve minority-group generalization in synthetic spurious-correlation settings.

record.problems: The paper's own memorization results concern synthetic spurious-correlation and regression settings and Waterbirds self-influence, not the original random-label image-classification setup. Figure-based results have no numerical values in the accompanying text; no uncertainty is stated for the memorization analyses.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version result was omitted. Table 1's subpopulation-shift benchmark comparisons do not directly measure a listed version; Appendix D's additional self-influence comparison is described qualitatively and adds GroupDRO to the Figure 2 comparison.

untested.parts: Deep-network fitting of completely random labels, associated chance test error, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Random-label versus true-label training time and convergence as label corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or entirely Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test error across a random-label corruption sweep.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting, and true-label generalization after removing regularization.
Deep-network learning trajectories demonstrating that real-data patterns precede noisy-label memorization. Section 5's qualitative regression narrative does not establish this result.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions; this does not dispute the reported effects on other constructs. The paper supplies no additional claim-version result requiring a missing entry.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random image labels, chance test error, and unchanged architecture or hyperparameters.
Relative training time for random versus true labels and convergence across corruption fractions.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or pure Gaussian-noise inputs.
A sweep from no to complete random label corruption and its effect on classification training and test error.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation affect random-label fitting or true-label generalization.
The specific claim that real-data patterns are learned before noisy or random labels, and that those labels are learned differently over training.

rows.subject: ERM-trained model
rows.value: Minority subpopulations show higher self-influence scores than majority counterparts.
rows.note: The paper interprets higher self-influence as increased memorization; no numeric values are stated in the text.
rows.check: Self-influence differences across correctly labeled subpopulations do not measure any listed version. The subject can be specified as a pretrained ResNet-50 trained with ERM.

rows.subject: MAT-trained model
rows.value: MAT shows a similar distribution for majority and minority examples, with overall lower scores compared to ERM.
rows.note: The paper says MAT reduced memorization while improving generalization; no numeric values are stated in the text.
rows.check: This is the proposed method's self-influence comparison with ERM, not a claim-version result. Exclude from claim evidence; the subject is a pretrained ResNet-50 trained with MAT.

rows.subject: ERM-trained linear regression model
rows.operation_detail: Fit regression model with example-specific features and label noise
rows.measure: Fit to noisy training examples and generalization to neighboring test examples
rows.value: The model learns the true function well, memorizes residual noise, and its predictions on a neighboring test example align well with the true function.
rows.note: The paper describes this as benign memorization; it is a regression setup, not random-label image classification.
rows.check: Fixed additive-target-noise regression does not establish random-label fitting or learning order in deep networks. Section 5 calls the models linear regression, but describes nonlinear predictions; retain this source ambiguity.

rows.subject: ERM-trained linear regression model
rows.operation_detail: Fit regression model with example-specific features and label noise
rows.measure: Fit to noisy training examples and learning of the true function
rows.value: The model may achieve zero training loss by only partially learning the true function and relying heavily on example-specific features.
rows.note: The paper describes this as bad or malign memorization that hinders generalizable learning.
rows.check: Partial recovery of a regression function is not a partial instance of any listed version. All Figure 3 models reach training loss below 10^-6. The source's linear-regression description conflicts with its nonlinear-function discussion.

rows.subject: ERM-trained linear regression model
rows.operation_detail: Fit regression model with label noise and no example-specific features
rows.measure: Training fit and generalization to new data
rows.value: The model may achieve perfect predictions on training data but fails to generalize to new data.
rows.note: The paper describes this as catastrophic overfitting and says early stopping generally can prevent it.
rows.check: Overfitting additive target noise without example-specific features does not test a listed version. The source calls the model linear regression while describing a highly nonlinear fitted function, leaving the model specification ambiguous.

rows.subject: ERM-trained linear model
rows.operation_detail: Train on synthetic data with spurious and core features, with no example-specific features
rows.measure: Training accuracy and generalization on majority and minority examples
rows.value: The model first learns the spurious feature, then adjusts its decision boundary toward the core feature and achieves perfect generalization on majority and minority examples.
rows.note: The text gives the sequence and outcome but no numeric training-time values.
rows.check: Learning spurious features before core features in correctly labeled synthetic data does not measure real-label versus noisy-label learning order.

rows.subject: ERM-trained linear model
rows.operation_detail: Train on synthetic data with spurious, core, and example-specific features
rows.measure: Training loss and generalization on held-out minority examples
rows.value: The model achieves zero training loss by memorizing minority examples using example-specific dimensions, and fails to generalize on held-out minority examples.
rows.note: The text attributes the result to the model not adjusting its decision boundary to the core feature.
rows.check: Memorizing correctly labeled minority examples through example-specific dimensions is distinct from fitting random or corrupted labels. Gaussian nuisance dimensions concatenated with informative features also do not constitute V3's unstructured inputs.

rows.subject: MAT-trained linear model
rows.operation_detail: Train on synthetic data with spurious and example-specific features
rows.baseline: ERM-trained model under the same setup
rows.value: The model learns invariant features and generalizes well in the presence of example-specific features.
rows.note: The text provides no numeric accuracy for this comparison.
rows.check: This is the proposed method's generalization performance compared with ERM, not a claim-version result. Exclude from claim evidence.

rows.subject: ERM-trained linear classifier
rows.operation_detail: Train on synthetic binary classification data with one core feature, two spurious features, and example-specific features
rows.value: ERM achieves only random-guess performance for minority samples.
rows.note: This is a result on minority samples in a spurious-correlation setup, not random labeling.
rows.check: Chance minority-group test accuracy under spurious correlations does not establish chance test accuracy after training on completely random labels.

rows.subject: MAT-trained linear classifier
rows.operation_detail: Train on synthetic binary classification data with one core feature, two spurious features, and example-specific features
rows.baseline: ERM-trained model under the same setup
rows.value: MAT nearly achieves perfect test accuracy for all groups.
rows.note: The text does not provide numeric accuracy values.
rows.check: This is the proposed method's group generalization performance, not a claim-version result. Exclude from claim evidence.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
